papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking Adversarially Robust Quantum Machine Learning at Scale
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections II.A to II.E (transferability, adversarial training, noise, attack detection); Methods and supplement skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study comparing quantum variational classifiers with classical networks under white box and black box adversarial attacks on image datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that quantum variational classifiers show notably enhanced robustness against classical adversarial attacks, by learning features that classical neural networks do not detect.
quotes: Our results show that QVCs offer a notably enhanced robustness against classical adversarial attacks by learning features which are not detected by the classical neural networks
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one simulation study; the abstract frames it as indicating a possible quantum advantage.
assertions.reader_inference: The result comes from noiseless simulation of one classifier family on four image datasets, so it does not establish robustness on hardware or for other quantum models.

assertions.value: The authors report that the converse is not true: attacks on quantum networks are also capable of deceiving classical neural networks.
quotes: the converse is not true, with attacks on quantum networks also capable of deceiving classical neural networks
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum variational classifier results are based on quantum simulations in a noiseless environment.
quotes: quantum simulations in a noiseless environment
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the setup and scope of its results.
assertions.reader_inference: Noiseless simulation bounds how far the robustness result can be read for current hardware; the paper itself reports that amplitude damping noise severely affects accuracy.

assertions.value: The authors state that their conclusion on adversarial training of quantum networks is based on the conducted simulations and that further studies may be needed to establish it in a fully general set-up.
quotes: However, we acknowledge that these insights
are based on the conducted simulations and further studies
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the limits of its adversarial training conclusion.

papers.title_in_file: Learning models of quantum systems from experiments
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, main text through Discussion; supplementary material skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A paper proposing a Quantum Model Learning Agent that uses Bayesian, unsupervised learning to recover a Hamiltonian model from experimental data, tested on an NV centre spin and in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that they propose and demonstrate an approach to retrieving a Hamiltonian model from experiments using unsupervised machine learning, and report success rates up to 86%.
quotes: we propose and demonstrate an approach to retrieving a Hamiltonian model from experiments, using unsupervised machine learning
finding success rates up to 86%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; the 86% figure depends on how the paper defines success.
assertions.reader_inference: The 86% applies to a set of credible models the authors chose, not to recovery of the exact model.

assertions.value: The authors report that in simulation the exact model is found in 60% of instances and the set of credible models in 86%, and that on experimental data the credible models are collectively found in 76% of instances.
quotes: the exact model is found in 60% of instances
the set of credible models are found in 86%
Experimentally, the credible models are collectively
found in 76% of instances
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; credible models are the authors' own success criterion.
assertions.reader_inference: The experimental 76% counts four roughly equivalent models as success; no exact-model rate is given for experiment in the quoted text.

papers.title_in_file: Generalization despite overfitting in quantum machine learning models
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 4 Conclusion; derivations in Sections 2 and 3 and appendices skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper characterizing benign overfitting in a class of quantum models via a classical Fourier features analogy.

assertions.value: The authors state that they derive the behavior of a classical interpolating Fourier features model for regression on noisy signals and show how a class of quantum models exhibits analogous features.
quotes: we derive the behavior of a classical interpolating Fourier features models for regression on noisy signals, and show how a class of quantum models exhibits analogous features
assertions.certainty_reason: Theoretical derivation for a simplified model class; the abstract does not mark it as a proof for general quantum models.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is an analogy for a restricted model class, not a statement about quantum machine learning models in general.

assertions.value: The authors state that they provide a concrete demonstration example of benign overfitting in a quantum model.
quotes: provide a concrete demonstration example of benign overfitting
assertions.certainty_reason: A single constructed example.

assertions.value: The authors state that they show an example of benign overfitting by a quantum model in a restricted context, that they do not consider a setting where the model is optimized with respect to a trainable circuit, and that future work may lead to more general characterizations.
quotes: While we have shown an example of benign overfitting by a quantum model in a
we do not consider a setting where the model is optimized
future work may lead to more general characterizations of this
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope and limits.
assertions.reader_inference: Trainable variational circuits, the usual setting in quantum machine learning, are outside the analysis.

assertions.value: The authors report in Table 5 that the quantum LSTM has MAE 0.0058 against 0.0116, MSE 0.000037 against 0.000147, and RMSE 0.0058 against 0.0116 for the classical LSTM.

assertions.value: The authors report that each epoch of the quantum LSTM required approximately 5172.22 seconds (approximately 1 hour and 26 minutes) in simulation, against approximately 0.41 seconds per epoch for the classical LSTM.
